predictions.title: Loader-verification chain ships training-to-tenant signed default by H2 2026
predictions.body: By H2 2026 the agentic-AI loader-verification chain reaches its end-to-end signed configuration as a default across the framework, serving-stack, and fine-tuning cohorts, with a single signed reference running from training-run checkpoint through agent-loader through tenant-policy attestation gate. The Tuesday catalysts are concrete and converge on consolidation rather than a fresh surface. A Tuesday arxiv release (2605.07735) extends the loader-verification line one further surface — from Monday's training-pipeline checkpoint-provenance extension to a tenant-policy-attestation surface, presenting a verification model that binds the training-surface signed-checkpoint provenance chain to a per-tenant policy-attestation manifest covering the fifteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter's tenant-policy field schemas. The paper is positioned as a third extension of the consolidated 2605.07241 framework after its 2605.07412 empirical companion and Monday's 2605.07588 training-surface extension, formalizing how the training-surface provenance chain composes with a tenant-policy-attestation manifest with only a marginal additional overhead. A Tuesday Simon Willison note characterizes the paper as the loader-verification line reaching its third documented extension within the May 16-19 four-day cluster, with the three papers plus the original framework now forming a unified four-document reference set the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment commitment can cite as a single coherent surface. A Tuesday andrew.ooo reading confirms the paper's reproduction harness extends the existing DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft consolidated reference-implementation index to cover the tenant-policy-attestation manifest, closing the loop from training surface to deployment-time tenant gate. The implementation cohort is already wiring the new hooks in: a Tuesday vLLM Blog operational note opens a v0.11.5 development branch that adds the training-surface checkpoint-provenance verification hook as a paving step on top of the existing five-surface mitigation set, a Tuesday Unsloth changelog confirms the optional training-surface checkpoint-provenance verification step is being wired directly into its router-only training driver, and a Tuesday InfoQ note reports the Mistral Workflows five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix conformance test suite now includes a training-surface checkpoint-provenance check folded in from the same arxiv extension. The structural force is that once the four-document academic reference set is unified, a federal civilian operational directive runs on the same eleven-CVE taxonomy with a Friday May 22 compliance window, the framework maintainer cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment commitment covers all five existing mitigation surfaces, and the serving-stack plus fine-tuning cohorts are already wiring the new training-surface and tenant-policy hooks into their builds inside the same window, the chain cannot ship in its bounded mid-June default-only configuration when both upstream surfaces are concurrently being instrumented across the same cohort. The most likely landing is the loader-verification chain reaching its end-to-end signed configuration as a default in H2 2026, with the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment shipping the five-surface bundle, vLLM v0.11.5 plus the next Unsloth release cycle plus the Mistral Workflows interop matrix general availability extending coverage to the training-surface and tenant-policy surfaces inside the second half, and the four-document arxiv cluster cited as the unified academic baseline. Bear case is that one of the two new upstream surfaces slips a release cycle and the H2 default-shipment ships training-surface-only with tenant-policy following in early 2027; absent that slip, H2 2026 lands the loader-verification chain end-to-end signed by default.

predictions.title: Microsoft, Meta, and AWS ship AI Services revenue breakouts by fiscal Q3 2026
predictions.body: By the fiscal Q3 2026 print cycle Microsoft, Meta, and AWS each carve out a discrete AI Services revenue line in a 10-Q footnote, following the Alphabet-led Q4 2026 cadence that the sell-side preview cohort has now hardened around. The Tuesday catalysts trace a tightening run-up to the May 21 Alphabet analyst day, now at T-minus-two calendar days. A Tuesday 247 Wall St positioning note reports Bernstein, Wells Fargo Securities, Evercore ISI, Citi Research, Jefferies, and Goldman Sachs Equity Research nudging the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability to 89 percent — a one-point uptick from Monday's 88 percent — with the cohort citing the unchanged Friday SEC Corp Fin fourth sample comment letter as the settled disclosure-precedent input. A Tuesday VentureBeat aggregation reiterates the cohort's consensus that Microsoft, Meta, and AWS follow with their own AI Services revenue breakouts in their fiscal Q3 2026 prints, with the Alphabet-led Q4 2026 print cadence unchanged. The capital-markets backdrop that the disclosure shift will price into is hardening on the same Tuesday tape: Cerebras CBRS holds the Friday $198.60 close as its reference anchor with the five-desk analyst spread bracketing the stock inside a roughly $185-to-$235 band, institutional-buyside cumulative net position edging to about 38 percent of float, and the May 21 analyst day treated by desks as the first session in the run-up where directional positioning typically firms ahead of a Mag-7 print catalyst. The Tuesday HPCwire AIwire note further reports Tenstorrent's SEC Corp Fin first-round comment-letter response at its twelve-business-day mark inside the staff-review interval ahead of a likely second-round letter, holding an early-August public-filing target, and SambaNova's bookrunner roster steady at six with confidential-submission filing target unchanged at the final week of June — a three-name AI-accelerator IPO pipeline that gives equity analysts a fresh public comparable set against which a hyperscaler AI Services line item is the missing disclosure piece. The structural force is that once one hyperscaler — Alphabet — ships a discrete AI Services footnote against a settled Corp Fin sample comment letter, peer 10-Q disclosure consistency under Reg S-K item 303 plus sell-side modeling demand plus a public AI-accelerator comparable set leaves Microsoft, Meta, and AWS with no defensible reason to keep AI Services bundled inside aggregate Intelligent Cloud, Family of Apps, or AWS segment revenue through another quarter. The most likely landing is Microsoft, Meta, and AWS each disclosing a discrete AI Services revenue line in their fiscal Q3 2026 10-Q filings, each citing the Alphabet precedent and the SEC Corp Fin sample comment letter as the disclosure-precedent input, with the sell-side cohort retiring the Alphabet-versus-peers asymmetry from its modeling notes. Bear case is that one of the three opts for a wider AI plus emerging-products bucket rather than a pure AI Services line, deferring the clean breakout into fiscal Q4 2026; absent that, the three-name cohort prints the breakout inside fiscal Q3 2026.

predictions.title: FMRB executive order signs with a parallel House joint resolution by end-Q2 2026
predictions.body: By end-Q2 2026 the Frontier Model Review Board executive order is signed and a parallel House joint resolution on the same 30-day technical-review track clears subcommittee markup, landing the United States' frontier-AI oversight instrument as a coupled executive-and-legislative pair rather than the executive order alone. The Tuesday catalysts are concrete and converge on a clearing-procedure sequence on both branches at once. A Tuesday Lawfare procedural note reports the classified-annex response clock advancing to its fourth calendar day with the deadline now at T-minus-two business days to the Friday May 22 expiry, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Director's office filing the second substantive submission against the Senate Cyber Subcommittee's classified-annex follow-up question set on top of Monday's first submission from NIST Director Locascio's office, and the remaining six witnesses confirming response drafts will land inside the deadline window. A Tuesday Just Security analysis restates that the classified-annex question set is the last remaining open procedural gate, observes that two of eight witnesses on record inside the first two business days is on the steeper response cadence the eight-witness slate had targeted, and confirms White House Office of Science and Technology Policy holding the line that the order remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology converted Monday's markup-scheduling decision into a calendar entry for the parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft, with the markup notice posted Tuesday morning per a PYMNTS Capitol-Hill note as the first formal House-track movement on the Frontier Model Review Board track since the order's signing window opened. The Tuesday CSO Online note on the CISA federal-civilian operational directive — now into its first full operating day with the Friday May 22 compliance window keyed to the same eleven-CVE Trail of Bits agent-loader taxonomy the executive order's technical review will lean on — establishes an executive-branch operational instrument the order can cite when signed. The structural force is that once the eight-witness classified-annex response slate is on a steeper cadence than the deadline requires with two responses already on record, OSTP has fixed no signing window before May 22 while leaving the post-May-22 window open, the House parallel-track joint resolution has a posted subcommittee markup notice on the same 30-day technical-review shape, and CISA has already published a federal-civilian operational directive on the same agent-loader taxonomy the executive order will reference, the order's signing compresses to clearing-procedure arithmetic — classified-annex close plus interagency-review close plus the post-deadline signing window lands the executive order signed inside Q2 2026 with the House subcommittee markup landing the parallel joint resolution inside the same quarter. The most likely landing is the Frontier Model Review Board executive order signing in the last week of May or first half of June 2026, the parallel House Energy and Commerce joint resolution clearing subcommittee markup inside Q2 2026, the CISA federal-civilian operational directive cited as the operational precedent inside the order's preamble, and the order plus the joint resolution landing as a coupled executive-and-legislative pair rather than an executive instrument standing alone. Bear case is a procedural slip from one or two of the remaining six classified-annex respondents pushing the signing window into early Q3 2026 with the House markup following inside the same window; absent that slip, end-Q2 2026 lands the Frontier Model Review Board executive order signed alongside a parallel House joint resolution clearing subcommittee markup.

reasoning.so_that: The FMRB executive order signs while a parallel House joint resolution clears subcommittee markup.
reasoning.landing: By end-Q2 2026; coupled executive-and-legislative US frontier-AI instrument.
reasoning.plain_language: The US AI oversight order is on track to be signed within weeks, and the House is moving its own matching bill at the same time.

By end-Q2 2026 the FMRB executive order signs alongside a parallel House joint resolution clearing markup.
